record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: For a nondegenerate indefinite quadratic form Q of dimension d≥3 that is not a multiple of a rational quadratic form, can one give an effective estimate T=T(ε) guaranteeing an integer vector x∈Z^d with 0<|Q(x)|<ε and ||x||<T?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 45 (G. Margulis [174]) . Give an effective estimate on T = T (ε) such that there exists x ∈ Zd with 0 < | Q(x)| < ε and ∥x∥ < T.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q$ be a nondegenerate indefinite quadratic form in $d \geq 3$ real variables, and assume that $Q$ is not a scalar multiple of a quadratic form with rational coefficients. By the Oppenheim conjecture (theorem of Margulis), the set of values $\{Q(x) : x \in \mathbb{Z}^d \setminus \{0\}\}$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$; in particular, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $x \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ with $0 < |Q(x)| < \varepsilon$.

Provide an effective bound: exhibit an explicit function $T = T(\varepsilon, Q)$ (depending in a quantitatively controlled way on $\varepsilon$ and on natural invariants of $Q$, such as its norm and a Diophantine measure of irrationality) such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $x \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ with
$$0 < |Q(x)| < \varepsilon \quad \text{and} \quad \|x\| < T(\varepsilon, Q).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The Oppenheim conjecture itself was proved by Margulis (1987), but the original proof is ineffective. Effective bounds have been obtained in special cases: Lindenstrauss–Margulis established an effective estimate for ternary (d=3) irrational indefinite quadratic forms with logarithmic dependence, and subsequent work (Bourgain, Ghosh-Gorodnik-Nevo, and others) has produced effective results for generic or Diophantine forms. A fully effective estimate valid for all nondegenerate indefinite irrational quadratic forms in dimensions d ≥ 3 remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Oppenheim conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Margulis' approach used the dynamics of unipotent flows on homogeneous spaces and was not quantitative or effective.
status_evidence.claim: The original Margulis proof is ineffective; effective versions remain a separate open direction.

status_evidence.title: Effective equidistribution and the Oppenheim conjecture (Lindenstrauss–Margulis)
status_evidence.snippet: Lindenstrauss and Margulis proved an effective version of Oppenheim's conjecture valid for all irrational indefinite quadratic forms in three variables, with logarithmic bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Effective Oppenheim is known for d=3 with logarithmic bounds, indicating partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Quantitative Oppenheim for S-arithmetic forms of rank 3 and 4
status_evidence.snippet: Quantitative Oppenheim conjecture for S-arithmetic quadratic forms of rank 3 and 4.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial effective/quantitative results have appeared in low rank and special settings.
